---
title: "Exercise: correcting sensitised emission"
---

## Goal

By the end of this exercise you should be able to:

- name the three images of a sensitised-emission measurement and what each contains,
- estimate the **bleed-through** $d$ and **cross-excitation** $a$ from donor-only and acceptor-only controls,
- compute the corrected sensitised emission $F_c$ and the apparent efficiency $E_\text{app}$ for a pixel or a cell,
- recognise false FRET from wrong coefficients, a forgotten background or misaligned images,
- explain why $F_c/I_{AA}$ and $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$ depend on the donor:acceptor ratio, and $E_\text{app}$ does not,
- estimate the noise of $F_c$,
- *(math)* derive $E_\text{app}$ from the forward model, invert the mixing matrix, and propagate the noise.

Do the pen-and-paper part first, then the demo.

## Background

| Idea | What it means |
|---|---|
| $I_{DD}$, $I_{DA}$, $I_{AA}$ | donor exc./donor filter; donor exc./acceptor filter (FRET channel); acceptor exc./acceptor filter |
| Bleed-through $d$ | donor emission seen in the acceptor filter, per unit of $I_{DD}$ |
| Cross-excitation $a$ | acceptor excited by the donor laser, per unit of $I_{AA}$ |
| Corrected signal | $F_c = I_{DA} - d\,I_{DD} - a\,I_{AA}$ |
| Controls | donor only → $d$ (slope of $I_{DA}$ vs $I_{DD}$); acceptor only → $a$ (slope of $I_{DA}$ vs $I_{AA}$); no-FRET → $F_c \approx 0$ |
| Slope through the origin | $\sum x y / \sum x^2$ |
| Efficiency | $E_\text{app} = F_c/(F_c + G\,I_{DD}) = f\,E$ ($f$: paired fraction of donors) |
| Noise (Poisson) | $\sigma_{F_c}^2 \approx I_{DA} + d^2 I_{DD} + a^2 I_{AA}$ |

## By hand

**B1.** **Coefficients from controls** (background already subtracted).
(a) Donor-only pixels $(I_{DD}, I_{DA})$: (200, 98), (400, 205), (800, 398). Estimate $d$.
(b) Acceptor-only pixels $(I_{AA}, I_{DA})$: (500, 52), (1000, 99), (1500, 149). Estimate $a$.
(c) Why a slope through the origin, and not an ordinary regression line with an intercept?

**B2.** A pixel of a cell with both labels: $I_{DD} = 400$, $I_{DA} = 500$, $I_{AA} = 1000$. Use $d = 0.5$, $a = 0.1$, $G = 2$.
(a) Compute $F_c$.
(b) Compute $E_\text{app}$, $F_c/I_{AA}$ and $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$.
(c) What would the donor intensity be without FRET?

**B3.** **A wrong coefficient.** Repeat B2 with $d = 0.4$ by mistake. Then take a no-FRET pixel with $I_{DD} = 1000$ (and $I_{DA} = 0.5 \cdot 1000 + 0.1\,I_{AA}$): what false $F_c$ does $d = 0.4$ give? How would you notice this in an image of many no-FRET cells?

**B4.** **Noise.** Assume Poisson counts (variance = mean).
(a) What is the standard deviation of $F_c$ in the pixel of B2? In per cent of $F_c$?
(b) Another pixel has the same $I_{DD}$ and $I_{AA}$, but $I_{DA} = 320$. Compute $F_c$, $E_\text{app}$ and the standard deviation of $F_c$.
(c) How many such pixels must be summed for a 10 % precision on $F_c$ in (b)?

**B5.** **Predict.** In a second experiment the acceptor is expressed at twice the level, everything else (donor level, binding, $E$) unchanged. Which of $F_c$, $F_c/I_{AA}$, $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$ and $E_\text{app}$ change, and by what factor?

**B6.** For each observation, give the most likely cause:
(a) all cells, including the donor-only ones, show a uniform positive $E_\text{app}$, and so does the background;
(b) the cells have a red rim on one side and a blue rim on the other in the $F_c$ image;
(c) $F_c$ in the no-FRET cells is negative, more so in brighter cells;
(d) cells with very high expression of both labels show FRET although the proteins do not bind.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solutions"}
**B1.** (a) $\sum xy = 200\cdot98 + 400\cdot205 + 800\cdot398 = 420\,000$; $\sum x^2 = 840\,000$; $d = 0.50$. (b) $\sum xy = 348\,500$, $\sum x^2 = 3\,500\,000$; $a = 0.0996 \approx 0.10$. (c) In a single-labelled sample there is nothing in the FRET channel without the dye: zero dye, zero signal. The model is a proportion. An intercept would absorb a background that should have been subtracted, and with noisy data it would trade off against the slope.

**B2.** (a) $F_c = 500 - 0.5\cdot400 - 0.1\cdot1000 = 200$. (b) $E_\text{app} = 200/(200 + 2\cdot400) = 0.20$; $F_c/I_{AA} = 0.20$; $F_c/\sqrt{400\cdot1000} = 200/632.5 = 0.32$. (c) $I_{DD} + F_c/G = 400 + 100 = 500$: FRET quenched the donor by 20 %, consistent with $E_\text{app} = 0.20$.

**B3.** $F_c = 500 - 160 - 100 = 240$, $E_\text{app} = 240/1040 = 0.23$ instead of 0.20. In the no-FRET pixel, $F_c = (0.5 - 0.4)\cdot1000 = 100$: false FRET proportional to the donor intensity. In the image, the no-FRET cells light up, the brighter (more donor) the more; $F_c$ plotted against $I_{DD}$ in those cells is a line with slope 0.1 instead of flat.

**B4.** (a) $\sqrt{500 + 0.25\cdot400 + 0.01\cdot1000} = \sqrt{610} = 24.7$: 12 % of 200. (b) $F_c = 320 - 200 - 100 = 20$, $E_\text{app} = 20/820 = 0.024$, $\sigma = \sqrt{320 + 100 + 10} = 20.7$: about 100 %. (c) Summing $m$ pixels multiplies $F_c$ by $m$ and $\sigma$ by $\sqrt m$: relative noise $1.04/\sqrt m \le 0.1$ needs $m \ge 108$ pixels, a small region of about 10 × 11.

**B5.** $F_c$: unchanged (it depends on the paired donors). $F_c/I_{AA}$: halved. $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$: × $1/\sqrt2 = 0.71$. $E_\text{app}$: unchanged.

**B6.** (a) Background (offset) not subtracted: an offset in all three images leaves $(1 - d - a)$ times the offset in $F_c$, everywhere. (b) The FRET channel is shifted relative to the others (misalignment, e.g. chromatic shift): at one edge $I_{DA}$ is too high, at the other too low. (c) Over-compensation: $d$ (or $a$) too large. (d) Bystander FRET: at high concentration unbound donors and acceptors are close by chance.
:::

### Math questions

**B7.** *(math)* Start from the forward model $I_{DD} = c_{DD}N_D(1 - fE)$, $I_{AA} = c_{AA}N_A$, $F_c = G\,c_{DD}N_D\,fE$. Show that $F_c/(F_c + G\,I_{DD}) = fE$, and that the donor signal without FRET is $I_{DD} + F_c/G$.

**B8.** *(math)* Write $(I_{DD}, I_{DA}, I_{AA})^\top = L\,(u, F_c, v)^\top$, give $L$ and $L^{-1}$, and verify $LL^{-1} = I$. What is $\det L$, and why does that mean this unmixing never amplifies noise the way similar spectra do in [lsunmix](../lsunmix/lec.qmd)? (Careful: what does amplify noise here?)

**B9.** *(math)* Show that at fixed $f$ and $E$, $F_c/I_{AA} \propto N_D/N_A$ and $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}} \propto \sqrt{N_D/N_A}$.

**B10.** *(math)* (a) For independent Poisson images, derive $\operatorname{Var}(F_c)$. (b) The coefficient $d$ is estimated with standard deviation $\sigma_d$ from an independent control. Show that it adds $\sigma_d^2 I_{DD}^2$ to the variance of $F_c$ across experiments, and evaluate the total for B2 with $\sigma_d = 0.02$. (c) Why does averaging over many pixels of one image not reduce this part?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solutions (math)"}
**B7.** $F_c + G I_{DD} = G c_{DD}N_D fE + G c_{DD}N_D(1 - fE) = G c_{DD}N_D$, so $F_c/(F_c + G I_{DD}) = fE$. The donor signal without FRET is $c_{DD}N_D = (F_c + G I_{DD})/G = I_{DD} + F_c/G$.

**B8.** $L$ has rows $(1, 0, 0)$, $(d, 1, a)$, $(0, 0, 1)$; $L^{-1}$ rows $(1, 0, 0)$, $(-d, 1, -a)$, $(0, 0, 1)$. Middle row of $LL^{-1}$: $(d\cdot1 + 1\cdot(-d) + a\cdot0,\; 1,\; d\cdot0 + 1\cdot(-a) + a\cdot1) = (0, 1, 0)$; the other rows are trivially rows of $I$. $\det L = 1$ (expand along the first row). The matrix is well conditioned for small $d$, $a$, so the inverse itself does not blow up. What amplifies the **relative** noise is that $F_c$ is small compared with the images it is computed from: its absolute noise is set by $I_{DA}$, $I_{DD}$, $I_{AA}$.

**B9.** $F_c/I_{AA} = G c_{DD}N_D fE/(c_{AA}N_A) = (G c_{DD}fE/c_{AA})\,N_D/N_A$. $\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}} = \sqrt{c_{DD}c_{AA}N_D N_A(1 - fE)}$, so $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}} = G\sqrt{c_{DD}/c_{AA}}\;fE/\sqrt{1 - fE}\;\sqrt{N_D/N_A}$.

**B10.** (a) $F_c$ is a linear combination with weights $1, -d, -a$ of independent variables: $\operatorname{Var}(F_c) = \operatorname{Var}(I_{DA}) + d^2\operatorname{Var}(I_{DD}) + a^2\operatorname{Var}(I_{AA}) = I_{DA} + d^2 I_{DD} + a^2 I_{AA}$. (b) $\hat F_c = I_{DA} - \hat d I_{DD} - a I_{AA}$ with $\hat d = d + \delta$: an extra term $-\delta I_{DD}$ with variance $\sigma_d^2 I_{DD}^2$ (independent of the image noise). B2: $610 + (0.02\cdot400)^2 = 610 + 64 = 674$, $\sigma = 26.0$. (c) The same $\hat d$ is used for every pixel: the error $-\delta I_{DD}$ is perfectly correlated across pixels and does not average out; it is a bias for this experiment.
:::

## Explore: three images, two controls {#explore}

A seeded field of eleven cells: donor only (cells 1 and 7), acceptor only (2, 8), free donor + acceptor without FRET (3, 9), a donor–acceptor fusion with efficiency $E$ (4, 6, 10) and "binding" cells where half of the donors are paired at $E = 0.4$ (5, 11), each with its own expression levels. True values: $d = 0.5$, $a = 0.1$, $G = 2$; background offset 100. Left: the three raw images. Middle: the corrected image (choose $F_c$, an index, or $E_\text{app}$; white = 0, red positive, blue negative), with the per-cell value printed on each cell (sums over the cell). Right: the scatter of the current control with your coefficient as a line. Below: a table per cell.

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../demos/dist/demo.css">
<div data-demo="threecube" data-preset="raw" data-layout="full"></div>
<script src="../demos/dist/threecube.js"></script>
```

**E1.** Preset **raw FRET channel: everything lights up** ($d = a = 0$). Which cells are bright in $F_c$? Read the mean $F_c$ of the two donor-only cells. Now press **remove bleed-through only**: which cells drop to zero, and which still show a signal? Then **remove cross-excitation too**.

**E2.** Press **measure d, a from the controls**. What values do you get? Look at both control scatters (buttons above the scatter). Read $E_\text{app}$ of each class in the readout and compare with the true $fE$ in the table.

**E3.** Preset **d too small: false FRET follows the donor** ($d = 0.4$). Read $E_\text{app}$ of the donor-only and no-FRET classes and of the fusion. Look at the donor-only scatter. Which cells show the most false $F_c$, and why?

**E4.** Preset **indices change with D:A, E does not**: the fusion cells now also express free acceptor (a different amount per cell). Switch between $F_c/I_{AA}$, $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$ and $E_\text{app}$ and read the three fusion cells (4, 6, 10) in the table. Which number is the same for all three, and why?

**E5.** Preset **low E, few photons: the difference is noise** ($E = 0.05$, 40 photons). Read the measured $d$ and $a$, the class values of $E_\text{app}$, and look at the $E_\text{app}$ image. Can you see FRET in single pixels? In whole cells? Raise the photons to 1000 and compare.

**E6.** Preset **one pixel shift: edges**, then **forgot the background**. Describe what each does to the corrected image and to the class values. Why does forgetting the background also spoil the measured coefficients?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solutions"}
**E1.** Raw: every cell except the acceptor-only ones is bright; the donor-only cells have mean $F_c$ = 157 and 88 per pixel (their bleed-through). Removing bleed-through ($d = 0.5$): the donor-only cells drop to about 0; the acceptor-only (17, 20) and no-FRET cells (18, 22) still show cross-excitation, and the fusion cells show 158–243. With $a = 0.1$ too: all controls are about 0, fusion cells 135–208, binding cells 72 and 56 (they differ by expression, not by FRET).

**E2.** $d = 0.499$, $a = 0.098$. Both scatters are straight lines through the origin with the fitted line on top of the cloud. Class $E_\text{app}$: donor only 0.000, no FRET 0.001, fusion 0.303 (true 0.30), binding 0.199 (true $0.5\cdot0.4 = 0.20$). In the table the individual cells agree with the truth to about ±0.005.

**E3.** Donor only 0.047, no FRET 0.047, fusion 0.326, binding 0.229. The line in the donor-only scatter lies below the cloud. The false $F_c = 0.1\,I_{DD}$ is largest in the cells with the most donor: cell 1 (mean $I_{DD}$ 313, false $F_c$ 32 per pixel) more than cell 7 (177, 17).

**E4.** $F_c/I_{AA}$: 0.539, 0.235, 0.480; $F_c/\sqrt{I_{DD}I_{AA}}$: 0.684, 0.452, 0.646; $E_\text{app}$: 0.303 in all three. The extra free acceptor raises $I_{AA}$ (the table's $\Sigma I_{AA}/\Sigma I_{DD}$ goes from 1.44 to 1.61, 3.69 and 1.81) without changing which donors are paired, so $F_c$ and $E_\text{app}$ stay; the indices divide by the acceptor amount.

**E5.** $d = 0.486$, $a = 0.097$ (noisier controls). Class $E_\text{app}$: fusion 0.055 (true 0.05), donor only 0.006, no FRET 0.006, binding 0.204. In the image single fusion pixels scatter by about ±0.08 around 0.06: the map is speckle, the fusion cells are hardly distinguishable from the no-FRET cells by eye, while the per-cell sums separate them. At 1000 photons the pixel noise is about 5 times smaller.

**E6.** Shift: the fusion cells get a red rim on one side and a blue rim on the other ($I_{DA}$ is displaced by one pixel); the class values change only a little (fusion 0.29) because the rims cancel when summed over a cell, but pixel values (and anything thresholded on them) are wrong. Forgot the background: the controls' slopes are pulled up by the offset ($d = 0.635$, $a = 0.411$), and then every class is wrong (donor only −0.058, no FRET −0.190, fusion 0.08). An offset is a component that is the same in all three images; it is not proportional to any dye, so a slope through the origin cannot describe it.
:::

## Where this leads

Sensitised emission needs two coefficients, a calibration factor $G$ and three images per time point, but works in living cells over time. The next unit measures $E$ from the **donor alone**, before and after destroying the acceptor: no coefficients, one end point. Spectral detectors replace $d$ and $a$ by least-squares unmixing of the whole emission spectrum ([lsunmix](../lsunmix/lec.qmd)).
